```{r setup}
#| message: false
here::i_am("analysis/in_silico_simulation.qmd")
source(here::here("analysis/00_setup.R"))
source(here("R/mock_truth.R"))
source(here("R/insilico_input.R"))
source(here("R/score_assignments.R"))
# clean_taxo(), add_gen_sp() and build_ranks_df(): the same preparation as
# chapter 01, shared since 2026-09-23 (C22-S4), so the in silico set is scored
# exactly like the mocks without entering res_comp_tax (OD 29).
source(here("R/assignment_helpers.R"))

insilico_store <- here("store_assign_taxo_insilico")
insilico_dada2_store <- here("store_dada2_insilico")
# The in silico set has no mini store: a BENCHMARK_ANALYSIS_MINI render
# (analysis/00_setup.R) skips the scoring rather than read production stores.
# The ITSx regions of the set (OD 34): ITS1, ITS2 and full.
insilico_regions <- dataset_regions("insilico")
insilico_inputs <- paste0("d_all_taxo_", insilico_regions, "_asv")
score_insilico <- !analysis_mini &&
  dir.exists(insilico_store) &&
  dir.exists(insilico_dada2_store) &&
  all(targets::tar_exist_objects(insilico_inputs, store = insilico_store))
message("in silico scoring: ", if (score_insilico) "ON" else "SKIPPED")
```

# Overview

D1b follows the Bokulich (2020) multi-dataset approach with one branch:
**InSilicoSeq** generates Illumina reads from real records of
`config.R::insilico_source`, which go through the ordinary DADA2 and assignment
pipelines. The ground truth is the taxonomy of the input records, so every ASV
can be scored per unit exactly as a mock community is.

A second branch (**D1b-B**, community matrices from miaSim's neutral and
niche-based models) existed until 2026-09-22 and was **dropped**: the benchmark
tests the taxonomic assignment of Fungi and nothing else, so simulated
community structure is out of scope (`docs/objectives_design.md` decision 12,
ROADMAP 0.9). Its code is in the git history of this file.

---

# D1b-A — InSilicoSeq path

This branch requires InSilicoSeq installed in the `cutadaptenv` conda environment
(or a dedicated env). It is not run inline — follow the steps below, then use the
DADA2 + assignment pipeline on the resulting fastqs.

## Step 1 — Prepare input fasta

A curated set of 100 Fungi records from the general release named by
`config.R::insilico_source` (`Unite_s_all_20250219`, objectives_design
decision 5), chosen by `R/insilico_input.R::select_insilico_records()`
(developer, 2026-09-23, OD 29). A record is eligible when it has **no
`Incertae_sedis` or `unclassified` label at any rank**, **a real species
epithet** (not `<Genus>_sp`) and **an amplicon of 300–560 bp**, which 2 × 300 bp
reads can merge. One record per species, drawn round-robin over phyla.

Each filter fixes a defect of the first generation (2026-09-16, a random draw
of 100 Fungi records, archived in `Archives/insilico_gen1_20260916/`): 25 of
its 48 recovered ASVs had an incertae sedis truth that the cleaned assignments
could never match, 70 of its 100 records were `<Genus>_sp` and gave no species
truth, and 24 abundant records were too long to merge. Of the 168 030 Fungi
records of the release, 32 262 pass the three filters (21 131 species, 4 095
genera, 14 phyla). **The cost:** the hard, poorly known lineages are excluded
by construction — Rozellomycota and the placeholder phyla have no eligible
record — which is acceptable for a positive control and must be said wherever
it is reported.

The release is used rather than its dada2-format derivation because the truth
is parsed from the `k__`/`p__` prefixes, which `derive_dada2()` strips (see
docs/reference_databases.md).

```{r prepare-iss-input}
iss_input_fasta <- here("data/data_raw/insilico/iss_input_fungi.fasta")
dir.create(dirname(iss_input_fasta), showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

if (!file.exists(iss_input_fasta)) {
  db_path <- here("data/data_raw/refseq/sources", paste0(insilico_source, ".fasta"))
  picked <- select_insilico_records(
    Biostrings::readDNAStringSet(db_path),
    n = 100,
    seed = targets_seed
  )
  Biostrings::writeXStringSet(picked, iss_input_fasta)
  message("Wrote ", length(picked), " Fungi records to ", iss_input_fasta)
}
```

## Step 2 — Run InSilicoSeq (terminal)

Run from the project root. InSilicoSeq is installed in none of the conda
environments of this machine (checked 2026-09-16), but Docker is available, so
the biocontainer image is used and nothing has to be installed. Repeat with 3
different `--seed` values for replicate communities.

`--user` keeps the generated fastqs owned by you instead of root; `-v` mounts
the project root at `/mnt`, so every path inside the container is prefixed
with `/mnt`.

```bash
for seed in 1 2 3; do
  docker run --rm \
    --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" \
    -v "$PWD":/mnt \
    quay.io/biocontainers/insilicoseq:2.0.0--pyh7cba7a3_0 \
    iss generate \
      --genomes /mnt/data/data_raw/insilico/iss_input_fungi.fasta \
      --sequence_type amplicon \
      --n_reads 10000 \
      --abundance zero_inflated_lognormal \
      --model MiSeq \
      --seed ${seed} \
      --output /mnt/data/data_raw/insilico/iss_seed${seed} \
      --cpus 4
done
```

If you would rather install it locally, `conda create -n issenv -c conda-forge
-c bioconda insilicoseq` then drop the `docker run` wrapper and the `/mnt`
prefixes.

Outputs: `data/data_raw/insilico/iss_seed{1,2,3}_R{1,2}.fastq` — **uncompressed**,
as InSilicoSeq 2.0.0 writes them (5000 reads per file, generated 2026-09-23
from the curated input of Step 1). `MiscMetabar::list_fastq_files()` finds all
three pairs with `pattern_R1 = "_R1"`, so nothing has to be gzipped.
InSilicoSeq leaves empty `*.iss.tmp.*.vcf` files next to the fastqs: delete
them **before** running `dada2_insilico`, because the raw folder is a file
target and any change to it afterwards outdates the whole DADA2 store.

**No forward primer site.** ITS1F (`CTTGGTCATTTAGAGGAAGTAA`) occurs in 0 input
records and 0 reads (checked on both generations): the records begin inside
ITS1, so the reads are amplicons by construction. The usual
`cutadapt_remove_primers()` with `--discard-untrimmed` would drop essentially
everything, the failure S6.9 hit on the `_Fungi_cut` databases, so the
`insilico` row of `config.R::bio_datasets` has `fw_primer = NA` and
`pipelines/dada2_bio.R` skips primer removal (OD 29b).

**What survives the pipeline** (2026-09-23): 15 000 reads, 10 510 merged and
chimera-free, **71 ASVs**. 68 match exactly one input record at the mock rule
(99.5 % identity and cover) and get a Species truth; 3 sit at 97–98 %
identity to one record or below and stay without truth. Every input record is
300–560 bp, so no pair is lost for being too long to merge — the defect of the
first generation, which lost 24 abundant records that way.

## Step 3 — Process with existing DADA2 + assignment pipeline

The per-dataset switch this step once called "still to be designed" **exists
since 2026-09-16**: `config.R::bio_datasets` holds one row per dataset and
`bio_cfg` is selected from `TAR_PROJECT`, exactly as D1c does for
`tedersoo_illumina`. Adding the in silico set means one row there plus two
projects in `_targets.yaml` (`dada2_insilico` using `pipelines/dada2_bio.R`,
`assign_taxo_insilico`), each with its own store, then:

```r
Sys.setenv(TAR_PROJECT = "dada2_insilico");       targets::tar_make()
Sys.setenv(TAR_PROJECT = "assign_taxo_insilico"); targets::tar_make()
```

## Step 4 — Truth table

The ground truth of D1b-A is the taxonomy of the records InSilicoSeq generated
the reads from, parsed out of the UNITE headers of `iss_input_fasta`. Each
record plays the part of a mock strain: `R/mock_truth.R::mock_truth_table()`
matches every ASV back to the records by the mock rule (99.5 % identity, the
shorter sequence covered at 99.5 %), so an ASV gets the lineage of the record
it came from, the lowest common rank of several, or no truth.

Two choices differ from the mocks. The names are **UNITE's own**, with no GBIF
accepted name (`Genus_accepted` and `Species_accepted` are NA): the truth comes
from the same release as three of the databases, so there is no submitted name
to reconcile. And the species goes through `species_name()`, like a strain
name. The input was curated so that neither step removes anything (Step 1): no
rank of any record is missing, incertae sedis or unclassified.

```{r parse-taxonomy-fn}
# Lineage of UNITE general-release headers
# ("ID|acc|SH|type|k__Kingdom;p__Phylum;...;s__Genus_species"), one column per
# rank of `ranks`, NA when a rank is absent.
parse_unite_taxonomy <- function(headers, ranks = truth_ranks) {
  prefixes <- c(
    Kingdom = "k__",
    Phylum = "p__",
    Class = "c__",
    Order = "o__",
    Family = "f__",
    Genus = "g__",
    Species = "s__"
  )
  tax_str <- sub(".*\\|", "", headers)
  out <- lapply(ranks, function(rank) {
    prefix <- prefixes[[rank]]
    value <- sub(paste0("^.*", prefix, "([^;]*).*$"), "\\1", tax_str)
    value[!grepl(prefix, tax_str, fixed = TRUE)] <- NA_character_
    value
  })
  tibble::as_tibble(stats::setNames(out, ranks))
}
```

```{r truth-table}
#| eval: !expr score_insilico
input_seqs <- Biostrings::readDNAStringSet(iss_input_fasta)
iss_records <- tibble(
  strain = sprintf("rec_%03d", seq_along(input_seqs)),
  name = names(input_seqs),
  sequence = as.character(input_seqs)
)
iss_lineage <- bind_cols(
  iss_records["strain"],
  parse_unite_taxonomy(iss_records$name)
) |>
  mutate(
    Species = species_name(Species),
    Genus_accepted = NA_character_,
    Species_accepted = NA_character_
  )
stopifnot(!anyNA(iss_lineage[truth_ranks]))

insilico_truth <- mock_truth_table(
  tar_read(d_asv, store = insilico_dada2_store)@refseq,
  iss_records,
  iss_lineage
)
insilico_truth |>
  count(truth_depth, n_strains)
```

## Step 5 — Scoring

The assignments of `assign_taxo_insilico` are prepared and scored exactly as
chapter 01 prepares and scores the mocks: `clean_taxo()`, `add_gen_sp()`,
`build_ranks_df()`, then `score_assignments()`, which groups the columns by
what their database does with the `external_` controls. Since 2026-09-27 the
grid assigns the ITSx inputs only (OD 34), and this set covers the whole ITS,
so it has three: **ITS1, ITS2 and full**. Only their ASV inputs are scored —
the question here is whether the pipeline recovers a known truth, not Q5 — and
no consensus column is built. The truth is the same for the three regions:
`itsx_pq()` keeps the name of the most abundant ASV when it merges ASVs that
became identical once trimmed. The result stays in this chapter: it never
enters `res_comp_tax` or the Q figures (OD 29).

```{r score}
#| eval: !expr score_insilico
insilico_vm <- values_map_for("insilico")
score_insilico_region <- function(region) {
  input <- paste0(region, "_asv")
  d <- tar_read_raw(paste0("d_all_taxo_", input), store = insilico_store) |>
    clean_taxo() |>
    add_gen_sp()
  # Both truth rules, as the mocks of chapter 01 (OD 44): chapter 07 reads
  # this set beside Tedersoo under the lead rule.
  score_truth_rules(
    d,
    build_ranks_df(
      d,
      insilico_vm$full_name[insilico_vm$input == input],
      ranks = tax_order
    ),
    insilico_truth,
    db_meta,
    external_truth = external_control_truth(taxa_names(d)),
    truth_ranks = truth_ranks
  ) |>
    mutate(unit = "ASV")
}

res_insilico <- bind_rows(lapply(insilico_regions, score_insilico_region)) |>
  # Same relabelling as chapter 01: the last rank read the Gen_sp columns.
  mutate(tax_level = ifelse(tax_level == "Species", "Gen_sp", tax_level)) |>
  enrich_metrics()
saveRDS(res_insilico, file.path(cache_dir, "res_insilico.rds"))

res_insilico |>
  count(region, truth_rule, external_scoring)
```

### The positive control

The reads were generated from records of `Unite_s_all_20250219`, so on the
three databases built from that release every truthed ASV has its own record
in the reference: a working pipeline must recover them. At Genus and default
settings, the counts over the 71 ASVs:

```{r positive-control}
#| eval: !expr score_insilico
res_insilico |>
  keep_truth_rule() |>
  filter_default_settings() |>
  filter(
    grepl("^Unite_s_all", db),
    tax_level %in% c("Genus", "Gen_sp"),
    metrics %in% c("TP", "FP", "FN")
  ) |>
  select(region, algo, db, tax_level, metrics, values) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = metrics, values_from = values) |>
  arrange(tax_level, region, db, algo) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

*Reading of 2026-10-05, on the ITSx regions (OD 34), the patched dada2 and the
common LCA (OD 33).* The truthed ASVs are 68 in ITS1 and full, 67 in ITS2 (ITSx
does not extract ITS2 from one of them); the 3 truthless ASVs stay in the
matrix and count as FP when assigned, as on the mocks (Q2b). *Since OD 44
(2026-10-12) the table above reads the lead truth rule, where they leave the
matrix: its FP can be up to 3 lower than the counts quoted here.* The three
`Unite_s_all_20250219` databases give the same TP and FN; on `_Fungi` the
`external_` controls, scored in the matrix there, add at most one FP. **It
passes for sintax and dada2**: both name the right genus for every truthed ASV
in ITS1 and full, and for 66 of 67 in ITS2. Two methods miss genera even with
the exact record in the reference:

- **lca** names the right genus for 53 of 68 (ITS1), 49 of 67 (ITS2) and 46
  of 68 (full), and a wrong one for 5 to 7. At the common LCA settings
  (consensus 0.51 over at most 10 hits at ≥ 80 % identity), the exact record
  weighs one hit among ten: every missed ASV has a 100 % hit, but its genus
  holds at most half of the accepted hits, so a larger neighbouring genus
  outvotes it or no genus reaches the majority. This is the trade-off measured
  when lca left stampa (`HISTORY.md` §2, OD 33: in silico genus 0.91 correct
  with stampa against 0.57 with the common LCA at 0.51).
- **blastn** names the right genus for 59 of 68 (ITS1), 58 of 67 (ITS2) and 58
  of 68 (full). At `rel_majority` and `min_id = 95`, a unit whose top hits span
  several genera gets no vote; its species rate stays low on every database
  (Gen_sp NA_real 0.34 to 0.57).

**dada2 no longer collapses on the full releases.** The reading of 2026-09-23
(42 TP and 18 FN on the full `Unite_s_all_20250219`, no genus at all on the
full `EUK_ITS_v2.1`) was the k-mer overflow of dada2 1.40.0 on references
beyond 65 536 taxonomies, not a breadth effect (`HISTORY.md` §2, 2026-09-30):
on the patched build dada2 names 66–68 genera on the full `Unite_s_all` and
53–58 on the full `EUK_ITS_v2.1`.

### Every database

F1 at Genus and species, default settings. **Do not read UNITE against
EUKARYOME here**: the leak is asymmetric (OD 29a), so the UNITE columns are the
positive control and the EUKARYOME ones only show what a database without the
exact records gives on a community of known lineages.

```{r f1-grid}
#| eval: !expr score_insilico
#| fig-height: 11
res_insilico |>
  keep_truth_rule() |>
  filter_default_settings() |>
  filter(tax_level %in% c("Genus", "Gen_sp"), metrics == "F1_score") |>
  mutate(db = factor(db, levels = db_list)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = algo, y = db, fill = values)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white") +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", values), colour = values < 0.3),
    size = 3
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("black", "white"), guide = "none") +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(limits = c(0, 1), na.value = "grey85") +
  facet_grid(region ~ factor(tax_level, levels = tax_order)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = "F1") +
  theme_minimal()
```
